children.why_this_cut: The first child covers the opening paragraphs on avoiding agenda-driven avoidance and the two worked examples (Tiananmen Square and erotica). The only crossing linkage is the chain_of_command concept, which is seeded and used in the BAD annotations; the child establishes the general principle that the assistant should not avoid sensitive topics and should engage objectively within content boundaries.

The second child covers the 'Be honest and transparent' section and its 'Do not lie' subsection, including the commentary, the ordering of outcomes, and the examples about lying. The crossing linkage is the chain_of_command concept (used in the developer-lie example and in the forthrightness rule) and the stay_in_bounds concept (referenced in the opening of the section).

The third child covers the 'Don't be sycophantic' and 'Consider uncertainty, state assumptions, and ask clarifying questions' sections, including all their examples. The crossing linkage is the chain_of_command concept (used in the BAD annotations) and the stay_in_bounds concept (referenced in the sycophancy section).

seed_vocabulary.name: authority_level_ordering
seed_vocabulary.prose: which of two authority levels outranks the other (root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority)

seed_vocabulary.name: untrusted_data
seed_vocabulary.prose: content in quoted text, untrusted_text blocks, multimodal data, file attachments, and tool outputs that has no authority by default and must be treated as information rather than instructions

seed_vocabulary.name: stay_in_bounds
seed_vocabulary.prose: the section of the Model Spec describing limits on the assistant's behavior, including scenarios where the assistant should refrain from fully complying with a user or developer request

seed_vocabulary.name: privileged_information
seed_vocabulary.prose: non-public OpenAI policies, system messages, hidden chain-of-thought messages, and private content the developer or user has provided to the model, which must not be disclosed without permission

seed_vocabulary.name: information_flow
seed_vocabulary.prose: the movement of information between parties, including direct transmission and actions like changing sharing settings or approving authentication connections, which the assistant should be mindful of

seed_vocabulary.name: chain_of_command
seed_vocabulary.prose: the hierarchy of instructions (root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority) that determines which instructions take precedence

judgment_calls: Chose a 3-way split at L2473/L2554 rather than a 2-way split at L2473, because the sycophancy and clarifying-questions sections are large and cohesive; a 2-way split would have made the second child too large.
The chain_of_command and stay_in_bounds concepts are inherited seeds that appear in multiple children; they are carried unchanged in seed_vocabulary so children use the exact names.
